Let the given matrix be $A$.
$$A = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10 & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14 \end{pmatrix}$$

The characteristic polynomial of a matrix $A$ is given by $p(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I)$, where $I$ is the identity matrix of the same dimension as $A$.

$$A - \lambda I = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10 & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14 \end{pmatrix} - \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Now, we need to compute the determinant of this matrix.
$$p(\lambda) = \det \begin{pmatrix} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

We can expand the determinant along the first row:
$$p(\lambda) = (-4-\lambda) \det \begin{pmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} - (-13) \det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} + 10 \det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the $2 \times 2$ determinants:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\det \begin{pmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(-5) = (-140 - 10\lambda + 14\lambda + \lambda^2) + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 140 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$

    \item $\det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (-9)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(12) = 126 + 9\lambda - 48 = 9\lambda + 78$

    \item $\det \begin{pmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{pmatrix} = (-9)(-5) - (10-\lambda)(12) = 45 - (120 - 12\lambda) = 45 - 120 + 12\lambda = 12\lambda - 75$
\end{enumerate}

Substitute these back into the expression for $p(\lambda)$:
$$p(\lambda) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(9\lambda + 78) + 10(12\lambda - 75)$$

Expand the first term:
$$(-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) = -4(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) - \lambda(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120)$$
$$= -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480$$

Expand the other terms:
$$13(9\lambda + 78) = 117\lambda + 1014$$
$$10(12\lambda - 75) = 120\lambda - 750$$

Now, sum all the terms:
$$p(\lambda) = (-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480) + (117\lambda + 1014) + (120\lambda - 750)$$
$$p(\lambda) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + (104 + 117 + 120)\lambda + (480 + 1014 - 750)$$
$$p(\lambda) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$$

The characteristic polynomial is usually written with a positive leading coefficient. We can multiply the entire polynomial by -1.
$$p(\lambda) = \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 341\lambda - 744$$

The final answer is $\boxed{\lambda^3+8\lambda^2-341\lambda-744}$.
